$comment: Phase 6.6 machine-readable HTTP API contract — canonical source (ADR-016). The JSON body of every operation is a JSON envelope in one of two classes: (1) dispatch envelopes produced by the Phase 6.5 boundary verbatim, kind=<operation name>, principal_id=<authenticated principal>, with freshness (possibly null), payload, evidence_refs and warnings on success or status=error + error + payload=null on dispatch errors; (2) transport-produced error envelopes — auth failures (401), method rejections (405), unknown routes (400) and the transport catch-all (500) — with kind="transport", principal_id="" and the same error taxonomy. HTTP status is the deterministic transport mapping in phase3.transport.errors and is never a replacement for the domain error code. This contract is validated against live runtime behaviour by tests/phase3/transport/test_67a_contract_reconciliation.py (drift fails there).

info.title: FIE reference read-only intelligence runtime
info.x-revision: phase-6.7a-contract-reconciliation-1 (reconciled to executable runtime behaviour; see ADR-016 and tests/phase3/transport/test_67a_contract_reconciliation.py)
info.description: Thin HTTP transport over the frozen Phase 6.5 IntelligenceService boundary. Read-only interactive plane (§3.5): only GET is served (HEAD mirrors GET with an empty body).

servers.description: reference defaults; operator-configured in real deployments

get.summary: Readiness — service initialised and persistence reachable (§10); maps to fie.health/get_health. No live Yahoo/TWSE/RSS fetch is required or performed.

503.description: dispatch error envelope (kind=health): DEGRADED/DATA_UNAVAILABLE/DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE — persistence unreachable; sanitised message

200.description: service + persistence status (envelope freshness slot is null on health)

503.description: dispatch error envelope (kind=health): DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE — persistence unreachable

200.description: scored intelligence items — the envelope payload is an ARRAY of items, each item carrying its own freshness; the envelope-level freshness slot is metadata for a SINGLE-item result and is otherwise null

500.description: transport catch-all INTERNAL_ERROR (transport envelope kind=transport) or dispatch INTERNAL_ERROR (kind=latest_intelligence) on persistence failure

200.description: entity intelligence envelope — NOTE: an unknown entity_id is NOT an error; the bounded honesty semantics (§8) serve 200 with freshness.state=UNAVAILABLE and an availability warning (NOT_FOUND is raised by the evidence endpoint, not this one)

500.description: transport catch-all or dispatch INTERNAL_ERROR on persistence failure

200.description: evidence node + related edges (exact node ref lookup — Phase 6.5 semantics unchanged)

500.description: transport catch-all or dispatch INTERNAL_ERROR on persistence failure

200.description: freshness envelope — every lifecycle state (FRESH/DEGRADED/STALE/UNAVAILABLE) is served honestly with HTTP 200 (§8); the envelope freshness slot mirrors the payload

500.description: transport catch-all or dispatch INTERNAL_ERROR on persistence failure

503.description: dispatch error envelope (kind=freshness): DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE — signal observations unreadable

bearerAuth.description: FIE_AUTH_MODE=token with FIE_AUTH_TOKEN (env-only, §6). Mode none = anonymous dev/test. In token mode the auth gate runs on EVERY path (including /healthz and /readyz, before routing); missing/invalid credentials → 401 below.

Error401.description: UNAUTHENTICATED (transport-produced: kind=transport, principal_id="") — token mode with missing/invalid bearer credentials; request-ID echoed in header and body

Error405.description: INVALID_REQUEST (transport-produced: kind=transport, principal_id="") — unsupported method; the interactive plane is read-only; Allow: GET, HEAD; request-ID echoed in header and body

Error500.description: INTERNAL_ERROR catch-all (transport-produced: kind=transport, principal_id="", sanitised generic message) — structurally reachable on every path via the transport catch-all; request-ID echoed in header and body

EvidenceRef.description: Stable db-agnostic evidence reference (phase3.service.contracts.EvidenceReference.to_dict): ref is the domain node id (entity:company:2330, signal:macro:global, …); kind carries the node type; edge_type/direction describe graph-traversal provenance and are "" when not applicable.

FreshnessMetadata.description: Phase 6.5 service freshness statement (ADR-002 governance mapping unchanged): FRESH=current known data, DEGRADED=inside warning window, STALE=past hard expiry, UNAVAILABLE=no observation. Stale data is never silently presented as fresh.

kind.description: the operation name (dispatch-produced: health, latest_intelligence, entity_intelligence, evidence, freshness)

request_id.description: sanitised X-Request-Id or generated hex; echoed in the X-Request-Id response header on success AND error paths

freshness.description: first-class metadata slot: a FreshnessMetadata object for single-result reads, or null when the operation has no single freshness statement (health, multi-item latest, evidence)

payload.description: domain data — object for single-result operations; ARRAY of items for latest_intelligence (each item carries its own freshness/evidence_refs/warnings)

kind.description: the operation name for dispatch-produced errors (e.g. latest_intelligence, readiness health/freshness), or the literal "transport" for transport-produced errors (401 auth failure, 405 method rejection, 400 unknown route, 500 catch-all)

request_id.description: sanitised or generated; echoed in X-Request-Id on every error path including transport-class errors and the catch-all 500 (never "unassigned")

principal_id.description: opaque principal label for dispatch-produced errors; empty string "" for transport-produced errors

message.description: sanitised — never contains stack traces, SQL, DSNs, paths, internal representations or secrets (§7)

x-envelope-classes.description: Every response body is one JSON envelope from exactly one of these classes (ADR-016):
x-envelope-classes.dispatch: produced by the Phase 6.5 boundary verbatim — kind=<operation name>, principal_id=<authenticated principal>; success = Envelope, dispatch error = ErrorEnvelope
x-envelope-classes.transport: produced by the transport for auth failures (401), method rejection (405), unknown route (400) and the catch-all failure (500) — kind="transport", principal_id="", ErrorEnvelope shape

x-method-behavior.head: HEAD mirrors GET on every declared path: same status and headers (Content-Type, X-Request-Id, Content-Length), empty body per HTTP semantics — implemented as do_HEAD → do_GET with body suppression; declared here instead of per-path head operations (single source, mechanically verified by the reconciliation tests)
x-method-behavior.non-get: POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE → 405 with Allow: GET, HEAD (read-only interactive plane, §3.5)

x-response-content-type.description: every response body — success and error alike — is JSON with this Content-Type (6.6R1 DEFECT-B contract)

x-auth-gate.description: FIE_AUTH_MODE=token: bearer authentication runs at the transport edge BEFORE routing — therefore 401 is reachable on every path including /healthz and /readyz; production deployments typically terminate auth at a gateway and permit the platform probes
x-auth-gate.canonical-401-behavior: 401 UNAUTHENTICATED, kind=transport, principal_id="", X-Request-Id echoed in header and body (never revealed credential detail)

x-http-status-mapping.description: phase3.transport.errors.HTTP_STATUS_BY_CODE (§7); DEGRADED is a freshness state and is served with HTTP 200 + metadata

x-transport-invariants: ChatGPT (any remote consumer) never accesses persistence directly (§3.2)
read-only: POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE → 405 with Allow: GET, HEAD (§3.5); HEAD mirrors GET with an empty body
no hidden live data fetch inside HTTP requests (§8)
never log or serialise Authorization values, tokens, payloads, or DSNs with credentials (§11)
